description: D-2026-09-20-07 / CLIENT-SDK.md's Application close row: the CLIENT calls its own application-close API (code 14 / APPLICATION_CLOSE) on a reconnecting client, and the reconnect loop MUST stop for good rather than redialing -- exactly one non-fatal disconnected on each side, then silence. This is the mirror of application_close.json (server-initiated 4014, where the client's reconnect loop is expected TO redial); here the initiator is the client itself, so redialing would mean the close API failed to reach the reconnect loop and merely dropped the socket underneath it. A short roundtrip first proves the connection was genuinely live before the client closes it. connect.reconnect.baseMs/capMs are pinned small (docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 1.1) only so a false-negative pass (an SDK that doesn't implement this yet and silently reconnects) would still show up fast rather than needing the runner's fixed 20s per-step timeout to expire on the first await; the await_none windows below (within_ms) are independent of these and set directly. The server's own initial `connected` (from the one connection RunPair's own setup makes) is never consumed by setup the way the client's is, so the first step below explicitly awaits and consumes it -- otherwise the later `await_none{event:"connected"}` would match that already-logged, unrelated event and fail immediately; consuming it up front means that await_none is really asserting 'no SECOND connected shows up'.
